Cc: linux-stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> # >= v5.6
Signed-off-by: Dinh Nguyen <dinguyen@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of a status property for the QSPI node in the device tree source files, which prevented the QSPI interface from being properly initialized and utilized by the system. Without the status set to "okay", the device tree would not enable the QSPI hardware, leading to potential failures in accessing flash memory.
